sources.title: Daniel Harlow, Jerusalem Lectures on Black Holes and Quantum Information, §§6.2.3 and 6.10
sources.locator: Full-text arXiv lecture notes; §§6.2.3 and 6.10, especially equations (195)–(196) and the immediately following discussion of homology, leading order, and the heuristic status of the proposal.
sources.reading_extent: The complete lecture-note text was retrieved. The full §6.2.3 dictionary discussion through its large-N and semiclassical-regime qualifications, and the full §6.10 RT/HRT discussion through its homology, leading-order, and heuristic-derivation qualifications were inspected; no claim that the entire source was read is made.

contents.name: §6.2.3, AdS/CFT dictionary and the separate semiclassical-regime question
contents.support: The lecture notes present AdS/CFT as an adopted correspondence and distinguish the dictionary from the question of when a good semiclassical bulk description exists. The local postulate keeps both as model inputs.
contents.limitations: This section does not derive the finite-regulator QES model or turn the finite sector identity into AdS/CFT.

contents.name: §6.2.3, large-N and semiclassical-bulk conditions
contents.support: The lecture notes distinguish a formal AdS/CFT dictionary from conditions for a classical or semiclassical bulk; they also caution that their general large-N criterion is not fully sharp.
contents.limitations: The postulate therefore treats its effective bulk regime and finite code data as supplied inputs rather than consequences of the finite matrix proposition.

contents.name: §6.10, equations (195)–(196), RT/HRT anchoring, homology, and least-area selection
contents.support: The source states the leading-order RT/HRT proposal with a codimension-two extremal surface anchored on the boundary region, a homology condition, and least-area selection among candidates.
contents.limitations: This is the classical leading-order proposal; it is not a proof of the local quantum-corrected dictionary, candidate existence, finite renormalized values, or general saddle dominance.

sources.title: Ahmed Almheiri, Thomas Hartman, Juan Maldacena, Edgar Shaghoulian, and Amirhossein Tajdini, The entropy of Hawking radiation, §§6, 8, 10, and 11.2
sources.locator: Full-text review; §6, equation (6.2); §8, equation (8.2) and its extremize-then-minimize discussion; §10, equation (10.4); §11.2, path-integral and cutoff limitations.
sources.reading_extent: The complete review text was retrieved. The generalized-entropy formula and QES explanation in §6, island formula and global-minimum discussion in §8, replica continuation in §10, and the complete §11.2 limitations discussion were inspected; no claim that every section of the review was read is made.

contents.name: §6, equation (6.2), generalized entropy and extremization followed by minimization
contents.support: The review writes the gravitational fine-grained entropy using a geometric term plus semiclassical bulk-field entropy, extremizes over codimension-two surfaces, and selects the global minimum. The local definition makes its own finite-regulator and convergence interface explicit.
contents.limitations: The reviewed formula is model-dependent; the local definition does not assert a universal continuum construction or existence of its limit.

contents.name: §8, equation (8.2), island contributions and minimum among extremal configurations
contents.support: The review states the radiation entropy as a minimum over extremized generalized-entropy values and explains that candidate islands may include zero or more disconnected regions.
contents.limitations: This section concerns selected semiclassical gravity-plus-bath models and does not establish the AdS dictionary for all boundary states or all gravity theories.

contents.name: §8 two-contribution Page-curve selection and §10 replica continuation
contents.support: The review describes selecting the smaller of competing extremized contributions and gives the replica continuation used in its gravitational entropy calculation. The local two-function cusp is proved directly from the stated minimum rule.
contents.limitations: The article's saddle comparison is not a proof that an island saddle contributes in a different model or that an exact finite-cutoff entropy has a cusp.

contents.name: §10 replica-wormhole assumptions and §11.2 path-integral, contour, saddle, cutoff, and exact-state limits
contents.support: The review describes the replica prescription and gravitational saddle comparison, then states that the precise path-integral contour, saddle inclusion, finite cutoff, and exact microscopic state remain incompletely understood.
contents.limitations: These qualifications delimit the review's model calculations; they are not a universal disproof of QES formulas.

sources.title: Ahmed Almheiri, Thomas Hartman, Juan Maldacena, Edgar Shaghoulian, and Amirhossein Tajdini, The entropy of Hawking radiation, §§8, 10, and 11.2
sources.locator: Full-text review; §8, equation (8.2); §10, equations (10.1)–(10.4); §11.2, unresolved gravitational path-integral contours, saddle inclusion, cutoffs, and exact-state limits.
sources.reading_extent: The complete review text was retrieved. The island prescription, replica construction and the stated §11.2 qualifications were inspected; no claim that every section of the review was read is made.

contents.name: §8 island formula and §10 replica derivation with saddle comparison
contents.support: The review describes island contributions, analytic continuation in replica number, and comparison of gravitational saddles in selected models.
contents.limitations: The article does not provide a universal, fully defined gravitational integration contour or prove that the same saddle contributes in every theory.

contents.name: §11.2 unresolved contour, saddle-inclusion, cutoff, and exact-state questions
contents.support: The authors explicitly separate semiclassical entropy computations from the still-incomplete exact path-integral and microscopic-state constructions.
contents.limitations: The discussion is a source-status caveat, not an assertion that no particular model has a controlled derivation.

sources.title: Phil Saad, Stephen H. Shenker, and Douglas Stanford, JT gravity as a matrix integral, §§1 and 6
sources.locator: Full-text article; §1 on the JT genus expansion and its non-unique nonperturbative matrix-integral completion; §§6.1–6.3 on ensemble dependence, non-disordered theories, and higher-dimensional questions.
sources.reading_extent: The complete article text was retrieved. The exact §1 scope statement and the complete discussion §§6.1–6.3 were inspected; no claim that all technical derivations elsewhere in the paper were read is made.

contents.name: §1 JT gravity as a two-dimensional genus expansion with non-unique matrix-integral completion
contents.support: The article states that its matrix integral supplies a non-unique nonperturbative completion for a particular JT gravity genus expansion.
contents.limitations: This result is specific to the two-dimensional JT model and does not establish a universal four-dimensional black-hole entropy law.

contents.name: §§6.1–6.3 ensemble dependence, non-disordered theories, and open higher-dimensional questions
contents.support: The authors distinguish ensemble-averaged matrix-integral results from fixed non-disordered theories and leave higher-dimensional ensemble questions open.
contents.limitations: This is evidence for a model-specific boundary, not a blanket claim that all island calculations are ensemble averages.

note: The A page has two independent full-text treatments, including Harlow's full lecture notes. Harlow supports the leading-order RT/HRT background; the quantum-corrected QES/island prescription and its replica assumptions come from the separate Almheiri et al. review. Saad–Shenker–Stanford is used only to delimit conclusions from a specific two-dimensional JT/matrix-integral model. No retrieval failed, no source was dropped, and no measurement or empirical observation is claimed.
